title: Two Knoxes, drummers Montague and Big Lord, and the hillbilly band
summary: Clarifying the two Knoxes, Montague and Big Lord at the Harmony Inn, and a hillbilly band that replaced them for two years.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Oh, you mentioned Knox from Baton Rouge. What did you say he played? Drums. Now, that's not the Knox. It's here. No, no, no, no. No relation even much.

Mm-hmm. See, now, this Knox, he lived in Baton Rouge now. He never comes to New Orleans, you know. And this Knox, they used to play, they played bass drum here. Mm-hmm. They went all together. Mm-hmm. No relation.

I just wondered. I'd forgotten about that. You've had several drummers down there, I think, too. I don't remember who's been there through the years. Where? At the Harmony Inn, now that I think about it. Yeah. Let's see. Did Montague play with you for a while?
He did, yeah. Montague played with me, too. Sidney Montague, yeah. Mm-hmm.
He comes back to you when you think about it.

Yeah, that's what I think of, yeah. Montague played with me until he got sick. Mm-hmm. And that's when Big Lord started with me. Mm-hmm. Then we quit there. We were off about two years. I went back again.
And that's why I went back with Big Lord again. Who was in there in those two years? Oh, a hillbilly band.
Which? A hillbilly band. Oh, a hillbilly band.
Yeah. Did you do okay with the hillbilly band? I don't think he did.
I had a lot of demands for me. People would ask me about it.
Then I, first I decided I was going to quit playing. We should go together. Because they just wouldn't let me. Step on work. Mm-hmm. When I went and played all day, I'd play someplace else. Uh-huh.
